answer: In an attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded random walks, limiting how far endorsements can travel. If a Sybil cluster has few edges to honest nodes, its external conductance is low; a min-cut then bounds how much stationary trust can cross that boundary. Under normalized voting weights, this limits the cluster’s aggregate influence unless it earns attestations from outside. Nodes named juniper, harbor, and quill illustrate that names alone confer no trust.
